extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals (PRSA members), chapter ethics officers, communications/ethics practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for ethical practice in public relations, including the PRSA Code of Ethics core values, BEPS role, Ethical Standard Advisories (ESAs), case studies, and related resources for resolving everyday ethical dilemmas.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA Code of Ethics — core values
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRSA Code of Ethics sets out principles and guidelines that uphold the core values of the ethical practice of public relations, including advocacy, honesty, loyalty, professional development and objectivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Code's principles (advocacy, honesty, loyalty, professional development, objectivity) to guide decisions and conduct in PR practice; BEPS provides education to explore these values year-round.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and acknowledge ethical issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizing and acknowledging ethical issues as they arise is among the reasons the PRSA Board of Ethics and Professional Standards was created.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should promptly identify ethical dilemmas in daily practice and seek guidance from BEPS resources, case studies, ESAs, or the BEPS Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEPS function — education, guidance, and code maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: BEPS upholds and amends, when necessary, the PRSA Code of Ethics and provides resources (case studies, Ethical Standard Advisories, quizzes, blogs) and educational opportunities to explore ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat BEPS as the primary interpretive body for the Code; use its materials (handbook, ESAs, case studies) for applying the Code to real-world situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Standards Advisories (ESAs) — force and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying the PRSA Code of Ethics, the PRSA Board of Ethics and Professional Standards offers analysis on current practice issues through Ethical Standards Advisories (ESAs). ESAs are considered direct extensions of the PRSA Code, and have the same force and effect as any provision within the PRSA Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an ESA covers a topic, treat it as an authoritative application of the Code for that area; ESAs are updated through a formal process to keep the Code timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure (ESA, 2018)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure (2018)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS issued an ESA on disclosure; consult that advisory for standards and examples about appropriate disclosure practices in PR communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and Social Media (ESA, 2015)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethics and Social Media (2015)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS guidance addresses ethical conduct on social platforms — attribution, transparency, representation, and other social-media-specific practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and Transparency in Native Advertising and Sponsored Content (ESA, Sept 2014)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure and Transparency in Native Advertising and Sponsored Content (September 2014)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises on transparent disclosure of sponsored/native content so audiences are not deceived about paid placements or promotional material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deceptive Online Practices and Misrepresentation of Organizations and Individuals (ESA, rev. June 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deceptive Online Practices and Misrepresentation of Organizations and Individuals (Rev. June 2012)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on avoiding deceptive online behaviors and misrepresentation; BEPS advisory applies Code principles to digital misrepresentation scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegal Recordings (ESA, March 2011)
rubrics_metrics.description: Illegal Recordings (March 2011)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses ethics/legal issues around recording conversations and the appropriate conduct when recordings may be illegal or unethical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Use of Interns (ESA, Feb 2011)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical Use of Interns (February 2011)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets expectations for fair and ethical treatment, supervision, and assignment of interns in PR environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism (ESA, Sept 2010)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism (September 2010)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines plagiarism and provides standards on attribution, original work, and how to avoid expropriating others' intellectual property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Looking the Other Way (ESA, Aug 2010)
rubrics_metrics.description: Looking the Other Way (August 2010)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises against ignoring unethical behavior; encourages proactive attention and appropriate reporting or remediation when misconduct is observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expropriation of the Intellectual Property of Others (ESA, Feb 2010)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expropriation of the Intellectual Property of Others (February 2010)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on respecting others' IP rights and avoiding use of protected material without proper authorization or attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Video News Releases as a Public Relations Tool (ESA, Oct 2009)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of Video News Releases as a Public Relations Tool (October 2009)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises on ethical use and disclosure when distributing video news releases to media and public audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questionable Environmental Claims and Endorsements (Greenwashing) (ESA, Oct 2009)
rubrics_metrics.description: Questionable Environmental Claims and Endorsements (Greenwashing) (October 2009)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards for honest environmental claims and endorsements; cautions against misleading or overstated environmental benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay for Play (ESA, Oct 2009)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay for Play (October 2009)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses ethical issues when financial arrangements influence coverage or endorsements and the need for transparency and disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engaging in the Use of Deceptive Practices While Representing Front Groups (ESA, rev. Oct 2008)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in the Use of Deceptive Practices While Representing Front Groups (Rev. October 2008)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises against deceptive representation through front groups and requires clarity about client identity and purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overstating Charges, Fees and/or Compensation (ESA, rev. Aug 2007)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overstating Charges, Fees and/or Compensation (rev. August 2007)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on accurate, honest representation of fees and compensation; avoid exaggeration or misrepresentation that would mislead clients or the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure by Expert Commentators and Professional Spokespersons of Payments or Financial Interests (ESA, April 2005)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure by Expert Commentators and Professional Spokespersons of Payments or Financial Interests (April 2005)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires disclosure of payments or financial interests that could influence expert commentary or spokesperson credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telling the Truth, Especially in War Time (ESA, Jan 2005)
rubrics_metrics.description: Telling the Truth, Especially in War Time (January 2005)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinforces the duty to tell the truth in high-stakes contexts and the ethical imperatives even during conflict or crisis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting Unethical Behavior or Unprofessional Performance (ESA, Nov 2004)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting Unethical Behavior or Unprofessional Performance (November 2004)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides guidance on when and how to report observed unethical or unprofessional conduct within organizations or the profession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Employment Status of Client-Based PR Agency Staff (ESA, May 2004)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of Employment Status of Client-Based PR Agency Staff (May 2004)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises transparent disclosure about employment relationships when agency staff perform work that could mislead stakeholders about independence or affiliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case-study topics and educational resources
rubrics_metrics.description: BEPS provides ethics case studies and discussion guides on topics such as Professional Conduct, Safeguarding Confidences, Looking the Other Way, Conflicts of Interest, Competition, Enhancing the Profession, Ethical Decision Making, and a Matrix of Ethical Dilemmas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use case studies and discussion guides to analyze real-world scenarios, practice ethical reasoning, and apply Code principles to specific fact patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content-specific issues — free flow and disclosure of information
rubrics_metrics.description: Content Issues: Free Flow of Information; Disclosure of Information; Disclosure of Deceptive Online Practices (from case studies/resources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uphold the free flow of truthful information and ensure appropriate disclosure when information is limited, proprietary, or potentially deceptive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital and organizational issues — representing front groups and deceptive online practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital Issues and Organizational Issues include Disclosure of Deceptive Online Practices, Representing Front Groups, and other online/organizational ethics topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid deceptive online tactics and misrepresentations of organizational identity; ensure transparency about clients and digital practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and categories of unethical/improper/malpractice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Code exists to inspire ethical behavior, clearly identify malpractice and other improper behaviors and warn and teach members how to avoid them. Unethical conduct is described as: a threat to the ethical practice of public relations; behaviors inappropriate or inconsistent with the Code; behaviors disruptive or that undermine ethical practices; practices and behaviors destructive to the reputation of practitioners, our profession or Society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these categories to evaluate conduct: determine if behavior threatens ethical practice, is inconsistent with Code, disruptive, or damaging to reputation — and respond with education/remediation rather than punitive sanction in PRSA's current model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-enforcement / education-first policy
rubrics_metrics.description: PRSA moved from enforcement to a strategy of education and inspiration: the 2000 Code revision ended sanctioning and identifying violators because voluntary codes are virtually impossible to enforce and can create legal risk for the Society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members should understand that PRSA focuses on guidance, examples, and education (not internal sanctioning); alleged misconduct may be better handled through legal or court proceedings if enforcement is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use BEPS resources (handbook, quiz, webinars) for ethical decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: BEPS provides a BEPS Handbook, Ethics Quiz (PRSA Ethics Quotient), webinars like “Ethical Public Relations: Everyday Expectations,” and other materials to test and educate practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ these learning tools to assess understanding of the Code and to practice applying ethical principles to common scenarios.
